question: Which is India's longest six-laned controlled-access expressway?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Agra-Lucknow expressway**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Agra-Lucknow expressway** is India's longest six-laned controlled-access expressway.
 
• This expressway spans approximately **302 kilometers**, connecting the cities of Agra and Lucknow in the state of Uttar Pradesh.
 
• It significantly reduces travel time between these two cities, boosting economic activities and connectivity in the region.
 
• The expressway is equipped with modern amenities and safety features, making it one of the most advanced highways in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Agra-Lucknow expressway** was inaugurated in November 2016 and is an important infrastructure project in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• It is part of the state's efforts to enhance road connectivity and support regional development.
 
• The expressway also serves as a crucial link to the Yamuna Expressway, further connecting it to the national capital, New Delhi.
 
• It features advanced traffic management systems, rest areas, and service lanes to ensure a smooth and safe journey for commuters.
